purpose: Sets the language and text direction of every Azion UI component below it. It wraps the app once, at the root, with the user's BCP 47 locale: components then read their built-in strings (close buttons, pagination, empty states, assistive labels) from the locale catalog and format dates, numbers, file sizes, relative times and plurals with `Intl` for that locale. English is built in; Portuguese (`@aziontech/ui/locales/pt-BR`) and Spanish (`@aziontech/ui/locales/es`) are separate entries the app imports and passes through `catalogs`, so an English-only app does not ship them. The catalogs are static imports, so the server and the client render the same strings and hydration never flips after the first render. Digits are Latin unless the tag picks a numbering system (`ar-u-nu-arab`): engines ship different CLDR defaults (Node and Chromium format `ar` with Latin digits, Safari with Arabic-Indic ones), so every `Intl` formatter receives the tag through `intlLocale`, and server and client render the same text. By default everything follows the person's device: an unset `locale` (and every component with no provider mounted) uses the device locale (`navigator.language`) for the `Intl` formats and picks its catalog when one is registered, falling back to English text. The server cannot know the device, so the server render and the hydrating client render `en-US`, and the device locale applies right after mount; an explicit `locale` (the user's saved choice) renders the same on both from the start. Only what people read follows the device: values that components hand back through `v-model` stay unambiguous (Calendar a `Date`, DateRangePicker ISO 8601 instants, TagEditor `key`/`value` pairs). It also carries the reference time of relative times (`now`), so a page that must render the same text on the server and the client, or an example, fixes it once instead of on every cell. The element it renders carries `lang` and `dir`.
useWhen: Once at the root of every app, with the catalogs of the languages the app offers; pass `locale` when the user chose one (`pt-BR`, `en`, `es`), leave it unset to follow the device.
Around one region that must read in another language than the rest of the page (a preview of an email in the customer's language).
To rename a built-in string for the whole app (`messages`), instead of passing the same label prop to every instance.
avoidWhen: Translating your own product copy (titles, descriptions, button labels you pass in) → keep it in your app's own i18n; the provider only covers the strings Azion UI ships.
Changing one instance's label → pass the component's label prop (`aria-label`, `confirm-label`); a prop always wins over the catalog.
Only flipping the layout for a right-to-left language → still use the provider with that locale; `dir` follows it.
related: `use-locale` — the composable components use to read the active locale, translate a key and format with `Intl`; use it in your own components to match Azion UI's formatting.
`pagination` — reads its labels and the "Showing x to y of z" line from the catalog.
`confirm-dialog` — reads Confirm and Cancel from the catalog when no label is passed.
bestPractices: Mount one `ConfigProvider` at the app root and pass the locale the user chose, or leave it unset to follow the device; do not nest one per page.

A nested provider changes only what it sets: every prop it leaves unset (`locale`, `catalogs`, `messages`, `now`, `timeZone`, `dir`) comes from the provider above it, and at the root from the device and the page. A provider placed only for `now` (a fixed sample clock) keeps the app's language, catalogs, overrides and time zone; `catalogs` adds to the ones above and `messages` merges over the overrides above.

Register every language the app offers in `catalogs` (`{ 'pt-BR': ptBR, es }`), imported from `@aziontech/ui/locales/<tag>`; a `pt-BR` or `es` locale with no registered catalog falls back to English and warns once in development.
Use a full BCP 47 tag (`pt-BR`, not `pt`); a tag with no registered catalog falls back to the same language, then to English.
Override built-in strings through `messages` (partial, deep-merged), not by forking components.

Leave `dir` on `auto`: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu locales turn the subtree right-to-left (a device locale does so only when its catalog is registered, so English text never reads right-to-left). With no `locale` and `dir` on `auto` the provider sets no direction of its own: its root carries no `dir`, so a provider placed only for `now` or `timeZone` keeps the direction of the page or the provider around it, and its components read that provider's direction.

Leave `now` unset in an app: relative times then read the real clock and `TableCellTime` re-renders every minute. Set it to a fixed moment where the text must not depend on when it renders: an example or a test (`const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 10, 10, 12)`, sample dates counted back from it), or a server render whose markup the browser hydrates. Never compute that moment from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup: the server and the browser read different clocks.
